scope: Independent source review of ERP console session fencing, encrypted command recovery, credential one-shot flow, UI state, permissions, task actions and associated XCTest source. Build/signing scripts are outside this review scope.

source.binding: Review applies to the exact file SHA-256 values below, not to an uncreated candidate commit or binary.

observedChecks.meaning: Whitespace check only; not Swift compilation.

observedChecks.reason: No Swift/Xcode toolchain in the local Linux environment; actual macOS CI required.

observedChecks.check: Signed IPA, physical iPhone and live ERP acceptance
observedChecks.reason: No candidate signing, device-installation or live-role acceptance receipt was available to this reviewer.

confirmedCorrections: Session generation and origin fence late login, refresh, reads and mutations; logout clears local authorization before network I/O.
Authority fingerprint excludes only the login-versus-me reporting timestamp mfaVerifiedAt. Actual MFA status and all other server actor fields remain binding; UI observes the full authority revision.

Encrypted immutable recovery binds original payload, version and idempotency key to origin, company and user. Persistence precedes the first mutation; retries are explicit and preserve original request bytes.
Known first-attempt atomic 422 NEEDS_APPROVAL/MISSING_CONFIGURATION rejections resolve recovery. A later rejection after an unknown result or restart retains the original command.

Credential commands use a fixed RAM-only one-shot whitelist, preserve password whitespace and revoke local session after submission. Generic credential-shaped payloads are rejected before journal persistence.

AES-GCM journal uses a distinct ERP directory and Keychain service, device-only unlocked key access, atomic protected file, backup exclusion and bounded reads. Corruption or missing key/file fails closed.

Navigation uses exact permissions and current server projections; OWNER/wildcards confer no invented client authority. Client/external Bauleiter portal records and own notifications/crew offers are reachable.

Pending retry exposes bounded original input/date/version. Successful task actions refresh current records; details use current items and contextual forms dismiss. BLOCKED/REOPENED start follows the existing transition contract.
Both loading-marker cleanup guards now include the UI epoch, so an old session read cannot clear a new session's loading marker with a reused read counter.
Redirect refusal implements the actual URLSessionTaskDelegate optional selector; its regression test invokes that selector without starting a network task.

openFunctionalLimitations.finding: Generic form input does not support null or union schema values. For example, site.geo_responsible.set can accept a non-null ID, but the form cannot encode JSON null to clear geoResponsibleUserId/onCallUserId. This is not full command-catalog parity.

user.invite and device.enroll return one-time token values that the generic result sanitizer hides. These generic forms do not establish a complete usable native invitation/enrollment handoff; a dedicated reviewed secret-display flow is still needed.

If the Keychain key exists while the recovery file is missing, load fails closed and login cannot complete its recovery read. This includes a partial first write or reinstall if the key survives but the file does not. No verified operator repair/reconciliation workflow exists; automatic key/file deletion would risk discarding an unknown operation.

An unknown original result followed by revoked permissions or a definitive later rejection remains pending and blocks new writes. The reviewed backend exposes no safe manual command-reconciliation endpoint; replaying with a new key or silently discarding the record is not accepted.

acceptanceBoundary: Static review accepts the bounded candidate delta for native validation. It does not certify compilation, XCTest PASS, full system parity, signing, real-device operation, production readiness, merge or publication.
